q7.answer: Each provider client calls the secret accessor on every request instead of copying the key in its constructor. The current value sits in an atomic reference that the 5-minute refresh swaps in only after a non-empty, well-formed check passes, so a request sees either the old or the new value, never a mix.

q8.answer: Before revoking, the check in Part B step 6 requires every running pod, including any leftover old-set pods, to log the new version id for all three keys. It runs only after a full 5-minute refresh cycle has passed since the last store write, and where the provider offers per-key usage data it must show no requests with the old keys. Whether per-key usage data exists is still open (open question 2).

q9.answer: The order is: (1) set store layout and access rules; (2) security issues new keys at each provider, checks them with a read-only call outside the app, then writes them to orders-api/prod/<name>; (3) move dev off live keys, which can run in parallel with step 2; (4) merge the runtime code and remove api_key lines from config/app.yaml in one merge, after step 2 and step 3; (5) roll out the new image; (6) confirm all pods use new version ids; (7) disable then delete old keys at each provider. The app switches to the store in step 5, and the committed keys are removed in step 4, in the same merge.

q10.answer: Dev keys are sandbox or test keys created at each provider and stored under orders-api/dev/*, and make run sets APP_ENV=dev so the app loads them through the developer's own identity, which has read and write on dev only. If a provider has no sandbox, the developer uses a local stub; prod keys never go on laptops and dev keys never go on disk.

q11.answer: The plan requires all three secrets to load before the app is ready. A failed load is retried (1 attempt plus 3 retries, 2 seconds apart), and after the last retry the app logs the error class and secret name, never a value, and exits non-zero, so the pod never becomes ready and the rollout halts while old pods keep serving. The plan does not separately say whether a missing secret gets the same retries as an unreachable store, so that distinction is not decided.
